KalixObjectStorageSpec defines the desired state of KalixObjectStorage.

A KalixObjectStorage is a namespace-scoped, project-level resource that declares
the named object-storage buckets (S3, GCS, Azure Blob) available to every KalixService
in the same namespace. One "default" instance per project namespace, mirroring KalixBroker.

audience.description: audience is the intended audience of the token, which will appear in the aud claim of the JWT.

expirationSeconds.description:
expirationSeconds is how long the token will be valid for. The token will be rotated when it is older than 80%
of this, or older than 24 hours. Must be at least 10 minutes. Defaults to 1 hour.

path.description: path is the path relative to the mount point that the token will be protected into.

issuer.description:
Issuer is the issuer of tokens that use this keyset.
If a token being signed or validated contains an issuer (iss) claim, this will be matched against it. This
allows multiple keysets for different issuers to be provisioned without conflicting.

Setting this parameter is also important if you have keysets from multiple issuers, but you don't trust that one
of them won't try and spoof the other. Since it pins a particular set of keys to only be used to validate that
issuer's token, if the other tries to spoof it, validation will fail.

refreshInterval.description:
RefreshInterval is used to control how often the keyset is refreshed.

This acts as an upper bound, if the source returns a Cache TTL (eg, via Cache-Control max-age), the shorter of
the two is used. Defaults to one hour.

jwksUrl.description:
JwksUrl is the HTTPS URL to load the keyset from.

Incompatible with useOidcDiscovery, secret and externalSecret.

useOidcDiscovery.description:
UseOidcDiscovery indicates that this keyset should be loaded using OpenID Connect Discovery, based on the issuer.
If this is true, then issuer must be set.

Incompatible with jwksUrl, secret and externalSecret.

allowedAlgorithms.description:
AllowedAlgorithms is the set of algorithms that are allowed for this keyset.

If the keyset doesn't define an algorithm, this will be used to restrict what algorithms are allowed to be used
with the keyset.

values should be forwarded as OpenTelemetry resource attributes on metrics and traces
emitted by this service. Each listed key must exist in exactly one of spec.labels or
spec.annotations — a key present in both, or a key absent from both, is rejected at
admission. Keys using reserved OpenTelemetry semantic-convention prefixes
(service., telemetry., otel., k8s., process.) are also rejected to avoid shadowing
attributes set by the runtime SDK.

keySets.description: KeySets are the keysets that should be used for JWT validation.

keys.description:
Keys that should be used for JWT secret configuration.
The order of this list is important. When signing or validating, the first matching key will be used, according
to the following rules.

For validating:
* The list is first filtered by all keys capable of validating - that is, any keys for the HMAC algorithm,
  or any keys for an asymmetric algorithm that have the public key defined.
* If the token being validated defines an issuer (iss), and there is at least one key that has that issuer
  defined, then the list is filtered to only include keys from that issuer. Otherwise, all keys capable of
  validating remain as candidates.
* The list is then filtered matching the algorithm. The algorithm only has to match by key type, that is, by
  HMAC, RSA, ECDSA or EdDSA. So a key that has an algorithm of HS256 can be used to validate a token signed
  by an algorithm of HS512.
* If at this point, there are still multiple keys remaining, then the first key that matches the key id (kid)
  parameter, if defined, in the token is used, otherwise, the first key of the remaining keys is used.

For signing:
* The list is first filtered by all keys capable of signing - that is, any keys for the HMAC algorithm, or
  any keys for an asymmetric algorithm that have the private key defined.
* If the token to be signed contains an issuer claim (iss), and there is at least one key that has that same
  issuer defined, then the list is filtered to only include the keys with that issuer, otherwise, all keys
  capable of signing remain as candidates.
* The first key out of the remaining keys is used.
Deprecated: Use KeySets instead

If this object is managed by a controller, then an entry in this list will point to this controller, with the controller field set to true. There cannot be more than one managing controller.

creationTimestamp.description:
CreationTimestamp is a timestamp representing the server time when this object was created. It is not guaranteed to be set in happens-before order across separate operations. Clients may not set this value. It is represented in RFC3339 form and is in UTC.

Populated by the system. Read-only. Null for lists. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata

generation.description: A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state. Populated by the system. Read-only.

resourceVersion.description:
An opaque value that represents the internal version of this object that can be used by clients to determine when objects have changed. May be used for optimistic concurrency, change detection, and the watch operation on a resource or set of resources. Clients must treat these values as opaque and passed unmodified back to the server. They may only be valid for a particular resource or set of resources.

Populated by the system. Read-only. Value must be treated as opaque by clients and . More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#concurrency-control-and-consistency

generateName.description:
GenerateName is an optional prefix, used by the server, to generate a unique name ONLY IF the Name field has not been provided. If this field is used, the name returned to the client will be different than the name passed. This value will also be combined with a unique suffix. The provided value has the same validation rules as the Name field, and may be truncated by the length of the suffix required to make the value unique on the server.

If this field is specified and the generated name exists, the server will return a 409.

Applied only if Name is not specified. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#idempotency

deletionGracePeriodSeconds.description: Number of seconds allowed for this object to gracefully terminate before it will be removed from the system. Only set when deletionTimestamp is also set. May only be shortened. Read-only.

selfLink.description: Deprecated: selfLink is a legacy read-only field that is no longer populated by the system.

finalizers.description: Must be empty before the object is deleted from the registry. Each entry is an identifier for the responsible component that will remove the entry from the list. If the deletionTimestamp of the object is non-nil, entries in this list can only be removed. Finalizers may be processed and removed in any order.  Order is NOT enforced because it introduces significant risk of stuck finalizers. finalizers is a shared field, any actor with permission can reorder it. If the finalizer list is processed in order, then this can lead to a situation in which the component responsible for the first finalizer in the list is waiting for a signal (field value, external system, or other) produced by a component responsible for a finalizer later in the list, resulting in a deadlock. Without enforced ordering finalizers are free to order amongst themselves and are not vulnerable to ordering changes in the list.

managedFields.description: ManagedFields maps workflow-id and version to the set of fields that are managed by that workflow. This is mostly for internal housekeeping, and users typically shouldn't need to set or understand this field. A workflow can be the user's name, a controller's name, or the name of a specific apply path like "ci-cd". The set of fields is always in the version that the workflow used when modifying the object.

uid.description:
UID is the unique in time and space value for this object. It is typically generated by the server on successful creation of a resource and is not allowed to change on PUT operations.

Populated by the system. Read-only. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names#uids

namespace.description:
Namespace defines the space within which each name must be unique. An empty namespace is equivalent to the "default" namespace, but "default" is the canonical representation. Not all objects are required to be scoped to a namespace - the value of this field for those objects will be empty.

Must be a DNS_LABEL. Cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/namespaces

deletionTimestamp.description:
DeletionTimestamp is RFC 3339 date and time at which this resource will be deleted. This field is set by the server when a graceful deletion is requested by the user, and is not directly settable by a client. The resource is expected to be deleted (no longer visible from resource lists, and not reachable by name) after the time in this field, once the finalizers list is empty. As long as the finalizers list contains items, deletion is blocked. Once the deletionTimestamp is set, this value may not be unset or be set further into the future, although it may be shortened or the resource may be deleted prior to this time. For example, a user may request that a pod is deleted in 30 seconds. The Kubelet will react by sending a graceful termination signal to the containers in the pod. After that 30 seconds, the Kubelet will send a hard termination signal (SIGKILL) to the container and after cleanup, remove the pod from the API. In the presence of network partitions, this object may still exist after this timestamp, until an administrator or automated process can determine the resource is fully terminated. If not set, graceful deletion of the object has not been requested.

Populated by the system when a graceful deletion is requested. Read-only. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata

the reference in the input string will be unchanged. Double $$ are reduced
to a single $, which allows for escaping the $(VAR_NAME) syntax: i.e.

exists or not.

appliedForceApplyGeneration.description:
AppliedForceApplyGeneration records the highest KalixOrganization
ForceApplyGeneration this service has already acted on. The operator
re-resolves org config and rolls the pods when the generation resolved
from the KalixOrganization (max over matching scopes) exceeds this value,
then stores the new value here so the force-apply is not replayed on
subsequent reconciles. Zero means no force-apply has been observed. The
audit (who/when/why) of the force lives on the matching KalixOrganization
scope's generic audit fields (LastModifiedBy/At + Description); the
management-api event log is the system of record for full history.

replicas.description: Replicas that are available for the KalixService.

lastAppliedRestartTime.description:
LastAppliedRestartTime records which Spec.RestartRequested value was last acted upon
for org config application purposes. When this matches Spec.RestartRequested, the
org config has already been applied for this restart cycle.

mappedImage.description:
MappedImage is the mapped container image. It may be different to the image configured in the container if
due to multi-region image mapping rules, the image gets mapped to something in the current region.

resolvedInstanceType.description:
ResolvedInstanceType is the instance type the deployment operator resolved
for this service via the chain: spec.resources.instanceType, then
KalixOrganization defaultInstanceType (scoped), then the platform default
"g1.general.small". Populated in canonical "g<N>.<shape>.<size>" form on
every successful reconciliation, regardless of which form was supplied
on input.

appliedOrganizationConfig.description:
AppliedOrganizationConfig is the organization configuration currently applied to this service's pods,
stored as a JSON string. This only changes when the service is restarted (via RestartRequested)
or on first deployment. An empty string means config has never been applied (first deploy/migration).
A value of "{}" means the org has no config but this state has been acknowledged.

NOTE: unsafe deletion ignores finalizer constraints, skips precondition checks, and removes the object from the storage. ServiceSpecJwtKey.description: KalixServiceJwtKey defines a key to be used for JWT signing or validation.

issuer.description:
Issuer is the issuer of tokens that use this key.
If a token being signed or validated contains an issuer (iss) claim, this will be matched against it. This
allows multiple keys for different issuers to be provisioned without conflicting.

Setting this parameter is also important if you have keys from multiple issuers, but you don't trust that one
of them won't try and spoof the other. Since it pins a particular set of keys to only be used to validate that
issuer's token, if the other tries to spoof it, validation will fail.

keyId.description:
KeyId is the id of the key.
The key id is required. When signing, it will be placed in the key id parameter (kid) of the JWT header. It may
be used for matching incoming keys when validating. It is important that, for a given issuer, if two keys have
the same id, that those keys must be the same key.

Ideally, key ids should be unique across all services.

The key id allows JWT keys to be rotated - a new key can be configured with a lower priority on all services
that use it, once that change is pushed out, then the keys priority (ie, the order in the list) can be increased
so that it is now the key that gets used for signing, and finally, once all JWTs signed by the old key have
expired, the old key can be removed.

algorithm.description:
Algorithm is the algorithm to use when signing JWTs.
When validating, this secret may be used if the secret for this algorithm is compatible with the algorithm that
the token being validated was signed with.

hmacSecretLiteral.description:
HmacSecretLiteral is an alternative for storing HMAC secrets directly in this spec.
This field exists temporarily until support for KalixSecret has been implemented. It is not recommended
for use, and will be removed at some point in the future. The HMAC secret should be base64 encoded.

exporters.description:

RouteSpecRoute.description:
Describes match conditions and actions for routing HTTP/1.1, HTTP2, and
gRPC traffic.

name.description: The name assigned to the route for debugging purposes.

prefix.description:
The prefix to match for this route.
If not specified, matches all requests.

enableWebSockets.description:
Whether this route supports WebSockets or not.
Note, enabling this will result in HTTP/2 traffic going through this route being downgraded to HTTP/1.1. This
may cause problems with gRPC.
Setting to true forces AllowStreaming to be true.

allowStreaming.description:
Whether this route allows streaming or not.
If true, this offers a hint to Akka infrastructure to tune routing for streaming.

consuming this KalixObjectStorage include this value in their reconciliation hash so that
a rotated credential — which changes the rendered config without changing the Spec —
triggers a rolling restart.

sourceType.description:
SourceType The Splunk source type: https://docs.splunk.com/Splexicon:Sourcetype
A [default field](https://docs.splunk.com/Splexicon:Defaultfield) that identifies the data structure of an [event](https://docs.splunk.com/Splexicon:Event). A source type determines how the Splunk platform formats the data during the indexing process.
Example source types include access_combined and cisco_syslog.

source.description:
Source The Splunk source: https://docs.splunk.com/Splexicon:Source
A [default field](https://docs.splunk.com/Splexicon:Defaultfield) that identifies the source of an [event](https://docs.splunk.com/Splexicon:Event), that is, where the event originated. In the case of data monitored from files and directories, the source consists of the full pathname of the file or directory. In the case of a network-based source, the source field consists of the protocol and port, such as UDP:514.

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the URL to a Splunk instance to send data to.

index.description: Index The splunk index, optional name of the Splunk index targeted.
